original_question: Are the numbers pi, zeta(3), zeta(5), zeta(7), ... algebraically independent over Q?
target_in_paper: Section 3.2, Conjecture 3.17: the k=1 specialization of the multiple zeta value discussion, asking for the algebraic independence over Q of pi and the odd zeta values.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's official statement almost verbatim: it singles out pi together with the odd Riemann zeta values zeta(3), zeta(5), zeta(7), ... and asks for algebraic independence over Q. This is exactly the content of Conjecture 3.17 in Section 3.2. There are no extra degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, or 'sufficiently large' clauses in this particular conjecture.
missing_details: Make explicit that zeta denotes the Riemann zeta function.
Replace the ellipsis by the indexed family zeta(2n+1) for all integers n >= 1.
If you want the question fully stand-alone, state the set-theoretic form: the countable set {pi} union {zeta(2n+1) : n >= 1} is algebraically independent over Q.

To stay paper-faithful, note that this is Conjecture 3.17 in Section 3.2, presented as the k=1 case of the surrounding multiple-zeta-value conjectural framework, not as a broader conjecture about all multiple zeta values.
refined_question: Let zeta(s) be the Riemann zeta function. Is the set of real numbers {pi} union {zeta(2n+1) : n >= 1} algebraically independent over Q?
justification: In Section 3.2 the paper first defines multiple zeta values and then states Conjecture 3.15 (Goncharov) and Conjecture 3.16 (Zagier) as the main conjectural framework for algebraic relations among them. Immediately afterward, the author specializes to the case k=1, i.e. ordinary Riemann zeta values, and states Conjecture 3.17: 'The numbers pi, zeta(3), zeta(5), ..., zeta(2n+1), ... are algebraically independent over Q.' That is exactly what your draft is aiming at. So the right refinement is not a broader question about all multiple zeta values, but precisely this k=1 specialization. The only real improvements needed are to define zeta, replace the ellipsis by zeta(2n+1) for n >= 1, and phrase the set whose algebraic independence is being asked about in a fully self-contained way.
